physiology:
The traditions seat this code in the pelvic floor, in the sacral plexus and the sex organs themselves, the part of the body where life is passed from one generation to the next. It is fitting. This is the code of intimacy, and the place it lives is the place where two bodies have always met, and the place where the line of bodies before you handed forward whatever they could not finish carrying.

The shadow has its floor here. The trauma the card names is not stored in the mind. It is stored low in the pelvis, in the tissues and the nerve bed below the navel, some of it from this life and a great deal of it older than this life, settled in the cells the way silt settles in a slow stream. The held-back inch the card speaks of is something the lower belly is doing. A tightness around the seat of the body. A quiet bracing in the very tissues that were built to open.

The climb out is also bodily, and it is slower than thinking. The pelvis begins to soften before the heart does. Breath drops lower. The bracing in the sex organs, the long inherited clench, begins to release in small involuntary increments while the mind is busy elsewhere. The card calls this transparency. The body calls it the floor giving way. What lived locked in the lower body for generations begins, in you, to move.
amino_acid:
Deeper than the organs, this code answers to a single amino acid, Valine. Valine belongs to the small group the body cannot make for itself. It must be brought in from outside, broken down, and only then put to use.

Valine has a quiet peculiarity. Unlike most amino acids, it is not processed first by the liver and then sent on. It is taken up directly by the muscles and the tissues themselves, metabolised out at the edges, in the body rather than in any central organ. The work happens where the body is, not in some governing room above it.

There is a teaching in that, and it sits well under this card. The work this code asks for is not done in the head. It is not even done in the heart. It is done in the tissues, low in the pelvis, in the very cells that have been carrying the wound. No central decision will finish this for you. The chemistry is local. The transformation is local. The pain is felt in the place it lives, and that is also the place it lets go.
